title: Food
summary: Food is necessary to feed your colonists and to breed horses. A new colonist is born whenever a colony has 200 units of food or more.

title: Grain
summary: Grains, such as wheat, rice and maize, are the most important source of food for your colonists.

title: Fish
summary: Fish is automatically converted to food.

title: Sugar
summary: Sugar is an effective sweetener and can also be used to produce rum, which achieves higher prices.

title: Tobacco
summary: Tobacco can be smoked or used to produce cigars, which achieve higher prices.

title: Cotton
summary: Cotton can be used to produce cloth, which command higher prices.

title: Furs
summary: The Furs of animals can be used to produce fur coats.

title: Lumber
summary: Lumber is required for constructing buildings and certain units, such as ships.

title: Ore
summary: Ore is necessary to produce tools, which have numerous uses.

title: Silver
summary: Silver is a valuable metal that commands high prices.

title: Horses
summary: Horses are necessary to create scout and cavalry units. In order to breed horses in a colony, you need some horses and at least one unit of fodder per turn.

title: Rum
summary: Rum is a spirit made from sugar cane. As a luxury good, it commands high prices.

title: Cigars
summary: Cigars are made from tobacco. As luxury goods, they command high prices.

title: Cloth
summary: Cloth is made from cotton.

title: Coats
summary: Coats are made from animal furs.

title: Trade Goods
summary: Trade Goods are only produced in Europe and are used for trading with the natives.

title: Tools
summary: Tools are necessary to equip pioneer units, as well as to construct advanced buildings and certain units, such as ships. They can also be used to produce muskets.

title: Muskets
summary: Muskets are necessary to equip infantry and cavalry units.

title: Bells
summary: Bells represent the colonists' desire for independence.

title: Crosses
summary: Crosses represent religious unrest in Europe.

title: Hammers
summary: Hammers represent the construction work carried out in your colonies.

title: Game
summary: The forest is home to many animals, suitable for hunting for furs or food.

title: Minerals
summary: The ground is rich in minerals, and for those who are patient, ore or even silver may be found.

title: Ore
summary: The earth opens up and a large vein of ore is available for mining. They are only found on hilly terrain.

title: Silver
summary: This mountain is well known to have silver veins, and will make nearby towns prosper.

title: Lumber
summary: This forest has good firm trees for harvesting lumber.

title: Furs
summary: An abundance of animals in these forests bring many hunters searching for easy kills.

title: Tobacco
summary: The soil of this grassland is exceptionally suitable for the growing of tobacco.

title: Sugarcane
summary: The soil of this savannah is exceptionally suitable for the growing of sugarcane.

title: Cotton
summary: The soil of this prairie is exceptionally suitable for the growing of cotton.

title: Oasis
summary: The oasis in the desert is a welcome sight for all weary travellers.

title: Grain
summary: Crops grow exceptionally well in this fertile plain.

title: Fish
summary: A high amount of small fish lure many big fish to this spot, which in turn lure the eager fishermen.

title: Plains
summary: Plains are large areas of land with relatively low relief, more suitable for farming. They produce a great deal of Grain, a lesser amount of Cotton, and some Ore. They are found in the temperate regions.

title: Grassland
summary: Grasslands are open, continuous flat areas of grass. They are often located near temperate forests in high areas or deserts in subtropical areas. Grasslands are ideal for growing tobacco. Food can be grown as well.

title: Prairie
summary: Prairie is an area of land that supports grasses and herbs, with few trees, and having generally a moderate or temperate climate. Prairies are most suitable for cultivating Grain and Cotton.

title: Savannah
summary: In savannahs, grasses and trees are co-dominant vegetation types. Savannahs are frequently seen as a transitional zone, occurring between forest or woodland regions and grassland or desert regions. Savannah produces mainly Grain and Sugar.

title: Marsh
summary: Marsh is a type of wetland, featuring grasses, rushes, reeds, typha, sedges, and other herbaceous plants in a context of shallow water. Marsh produces some Grain and Tobacco, as well as Ore. Marshes are mainly found near the polar regions.

title: Swamp
summary: Tropical wetlands by shallow bodies of water. Swamps have a greater proportion of open water surface and generally deeper than marshes. Swamp yields some Grain, as well as small amounts of Sugar and Ore.

title: Desert
summary: Deserts are very dry, they receive minimal precipitation. Though scarce, deserts produce Grain, Cotton and Ore.

title: Tundra
summary: Tundra is an area where the tree growth is hindered by low temperatures and short growing seasons. Tundra produces Grain and some Ore. It is found near the polar regions.

title: Mixed forest
summary: Mixed forests, which can be found in the temperate latitudes, produce Grain, Lumber, Furs, and some Cotton. If mixed forests are cleared, they become plains.

title: Conifer forest
summary: Conifer forests produce Grain, Lumber, Furs, and some Tobacco. They are found mainly in the tropical latitudes and give way to grassland when cleared.

title: Broadleaf forest
summary: Broadleaf forests produce Grain, Lumber, Furs, and some Cotton. They are found in the temperate latitudes and give way to prairies when cleared.

title: Tropical forest
summary: Tropical forests produce Grain, Lumber, Furs, and some Sugar. Clearing tropical forests produces savannah.

title: Wetland forest
summary: Wetland forests produce Grain, Lumber, Furs, and some Ore. Wetland forests can be cleared to produce marsh land. They are found near the polar regions.

title: Rain forest
summary: Rain forests produce Grain, Lumber, Furs, and some Ore and Sugar. They are found in the tropics and can be cleared to produce swamps.

title: Scrub forest
summary: Scrub forests produce Grain, Lumber, Furs, and some Cotton and Ore. If they are cleared, the land becomes a desert. Scrub forests are found in temperate regions.

title: Boreal forest
summary: Boreal forests produce Grain, Lumber, Furs, and some Ore. They are found near the polar regions and can be cleared to produce tundra.

title: Hills
summary: Hills extend above the surrounding terrain, in a limited area. Hills produce a large amount of Ore, as well as some Grain.

title: Mountains
summary: Mountains extend above the surrounding terrain in a limited area. Mountains are generally steeper than hills. They are difficult to travel and colonies cannot be founded here. They provide a high defensive bonus but fortification does not increase this. Mining proves useful for ore and silver extraction.

title: Arctic
summary: Arctic is mostly a vast, ice-covered ocean surrounded by treeless, frozen ground and produce nothing. They are found near the North and South Pole and can not usually support colonies.

title: Ocean
summary: Oceans are major bodies of saline water, good for fishing. The amount of fish is increased by the presence of land and especially by river mouths.

title: Lake
summary: Lakes are inland bodies of water. Colonies built adjacently profit from the lakes natural resources, but may be inaccessible via ship.

title: High seas
summary: High seas produce Fish. They also enable your ships to sail to and from Europe.

title: Great river
summary: Great rivers are rivers that can be navigated by ships.

title: River
summary: River

title: Road
summary: Road

title: Plow
summary: Plowed

title: Fish bonus (coast)
summary: Fish bonus due to land nearby

title: Fish bonus (river)
summary: Fish bonus due to a river

title: Free Colonist
summary: The Free Colonist is a greenhorn without any particular skills. However, Free Colonists can become skilled units by working on your colony tiles, or by visiting Indian settlements. They can also be promoted to Veteran Soldiers, or educated in colonies that have built a school.

title: Expert Farmer
summary: The Expert Farmer is a specialist at producing food.

title: Expert Fisherman
summary: The Expert Fisherman is a specialist at catching fish, which are automatically converted to food.

title: Expert Fur Trapper
summary: The Expert Fur Trapper specialises in producing furs.

title: Expert Silver Miner
summary: The Expert Silver Miner produces more silver than any other unit.

title: Expert Lumberjack
summary: The Expert Lumberjack cuts down trees to produce lumber.

title: Expert Ore Miner
summary: The Expert Ore Miner excels at mining ore.

title: Master Sugar Planter
summary: The Master Sugar Planter cultivates sugar.

title: Master Cotton Planter
summary: The Master Cotton Planter cultivates cotton.

title: Master Tobacco Planter
summary: The Master Tobacco Planter cultivates tobacco.

title: Firebrand Preacher
summary: The Firebrand Preacher increases religious unrest in Europe (symbolised by Crosses), which in turn increases emigration to the New World.

title: Elder Statesman
summary: The Elder Statesman increases the colonists' desire for independence (symbolised by Liberty Bells), which increases the Sons of Liberty membership in your colonies.

title: Master Carpenter
summary: The Master Carpenter is particularly skilled at producing buildings and units in your colonies.

title: Master Distiller
summary: The Master Distiller uses sugar to produce rum.

title: Master Weaver
summary: The Master Weaver turns cotton into cloth.

title: Master Tobacconist
summary: The Master Tobacconist makes cigars from tobacco.

title: Master Fur Trader
summary: The Master Fur Trader turns furs into coats.

title: Master Blacksmith
summary: The Master Blacksmith forges tools from ore.

title: Master Gunsmith
summary: The Master Gunsmith uses tools to produce muskets.

title: Seasoned Scout
summary: The Seasoned Scout is best at exploring the New World, particularly Indian settlements and Lost City Rumours.

title: Hardy Pioneer
summary: The Hardy Pioneer excels at clearing forests, plowing fields and building roads.

title: Veteran Soldier
summary: The Veteran Soldier is an experienced military unit. Any Free Colonist may be promoted to a Veteran Soldier after winning a battle.

title: Jesuit Missionary
summary: The Jesuit Missionary is able to establish a mission in an Indian settlement and is especially skilled at converting Indians.

title: Indentured Servant
summary: The Indentured Servant is well suited for outdoor work, but less suited for indoor work. He may become a Free Colonist through promotion or education.

title: Petty Criminal
summary: The Petty Criminal is suited for outdoor work, but unsuited for indoor work. He may become an Indentured Servant through promotion or education.

title: Indian Convert
summary: The Indian Convert is a native who has joined one of your colonies. He is skilled at all kinds of outdoor work, but unskilled at indoor work. As soon as Bartolome de las Casas joins the Continental Congress, all Indian Converts become Free Colonists.

title: Brave
summary: The Brave is a native unit able to carry a small amount of goods. He may be armed and mounted. Braves often visit your colonies in order to bring you gifts or make demands.

title: Colonial Regular
summary: The Colonial Regular is a crack unit only available after the Declaration of Independence.

title: King's Regular
summary: The King's Regular is a crack unit only available to the Crown. You will see them only when the Royal Expeditionary Force arrives after the Declaration of Independence.

title: Caravel
summary: The Caravel is a small and not particularly fast merchant ship.

title: Frigate
summary: The Frigate is a small warship.

title: Galleon
summary: The Galleon is a large merchant ship. It is the only ship able to take a Treasure Train to Europe.

title: Man of War
summary: The Man of War is a large warship. It is only available to the Crown and after the Declaration of Independence.

title: Merchantman
summary: The Merchantman is a medium-sized merchant ship.

title: Privateer
summary: The Privateer is a small warship that does not fly the flag of the country it hails from. It is the only unit able to attack other units without declaring war.

title: Artillery
summary: Artillery is good at attacking and defending colonies, and very vulnerable in the open.

title: Damaged Artillery
summary: Damaged Artillery is like Artillery in every way, only weaker.

title: Treasure Train
summary: The sole purpose of the Treasure Train is to transport the gold found in the ruins of a Lost City, or plundered from an Indian settlement. If you move it into one of your colonies, the Crown will offer to transport it to Europe for a reasonable fee. If you have a Galleon, you can move it to Europe yourself.

title: Wagon Train
summary: The Wagon Train is able to carry up to 200 units of goods over land. You can use it to trade with other players, or to move goods between your own colonies.

title: The Captain
summary: The Captain has sold his soul to the Devil.

title: The Flying Dutchman
summary: The Flying Dutchman is the ship of the damned.

title: Undead
summary: The Undead are the crew of the Flying Dutchman.

title: Town Hall
summary: The town Hall, which can not be upgraded, provides workplaces for up to three colonists producing liberty bells. Its effect can be increased by building a printing press and a newspaper.

title: Carpenter's house
summary: The carpenter's house, which can be upgraded to a lumber mill once the colony's population reaches 3, is used to convert lumber to hammers. Hammers are required to construct or upgrade all kinds of buildings.

title: Lumber mill
summary: The lumber mill, which can not be upgraded, is used to convert lumber to hammers. Hammers are required to construct or upgrade all kinds of buildings. A lumber mill increases hammer production.

title: Blacksmith's house
summary: The blacksmith's house, which can be upgraded to a blacksmith's shop, is used to convert ore to tools. Tools are required to construct certain kinds of buildings and to upgrade all kinds of buildings. Tools are also used by pioneers and to produce muskets. Once the population of the colony has reached 8, the blacksmith's shop can be replaced by an iron works, provided that Adam Smith has joined the Continental Congress.

title: Blacksmith's shop
summary: The blacksmith's shop, which can be upgraded to an iron works, is used to convert ore to tools. Tools are required to construct certain kinds of buildings and to upgrade all kinds of buildings. Tools are also used by pioneers and to produce muskets. Once the population of the colony has reached 8, the blacksmith's shop can be replaced by an iron works, provided that Adam Smith has joined the Continental Congress. A blacksmith's shop increases tool production.

title: Iron works
summary: The iron works, which can not be upgraded, is used to convert ore to tools. Tools are required to construct certain kinds of buildings and to upgrade all kinds of buildings. Tools are also used by pioneers and to produce muskets. An iron works increases tool production.

title: Tobacconist's house
summary: The tobacconist's house, which can be upgraded to a tobacconist's shop, is used to produce cigars from tobacco. Once the colony's population has reached 8, it can be further upgraded to a cigar factory, provided that Adam Smith has joined the Continental Congress.

title: Tobacconist's shop
summary: The tobacconist's shop, which can be upgraded to a cigar factory, is used to produce cigars from tobacco. Once the colony's population has reached 8, it can be further upgraded to a cigar factory, provided that Adam Smith has joined the Continental Congress. A tobacconist's shop increases cigar production.

title: Cigar factory
summary: The cigar factory, which can not be upgraded, is used to produce cigars from tobacco. A cigar factory increases cigar production.

title: Weaver's house
summary: The weaver's house, which can be upgraded to a weaver's shop, is used to turn cotton into cloth. It can be upgraded to a textile mill as soon as the population of the colony is at least 8 and Adam Smith has joined the Continental Congress.

title: Weaver's shop
summary: The weaver's shop, which can be upgraded to a textile mill, is used to turn cotton into cloth. It can be upgraded to a textile mill as soon as the population of the colony is at least 8 and Adam Smith has joined the Continental Congress. A weaver's shop increases cloth production.

title: Textile mill
summary: The textile mill, which can not be upgraded, is used to turn cotton into cloth. A textile mill increases cloth production.

title: Distiller's house
summary: The distiller's house, which can be upgraded to a rum distillery, is used to produce rum from sugar. Once Adam Smith has joined the Continental Congress and the colony's population is at least 8, the rum distillery can be replaced by a rum factory.

title: Rum distillery
summary: The rum distillery, which can be upgraded to a rum factory, is used to produce rum from sugar. Once Adam Smith has joined the Continental Congress and the colony's population is at least 8, the rum distillery can be replaced by a rum factory. A rum distillery increases rum production.

title: Rum factory
summary: The rum factory, which can not be upgraded, is used to produce rum from sugar. A rum factory increases rum production.

title: Fur trader's house
summary: The fur trader's house, which can be upgraded to a fur trader's post, is used to produce coats from furs. Once the colony's population has reached 6, it can be further upgraded to a fur factory, provided that Adam Smith has joined the Continental Congress.

title: Fur trading post
summary: The fur trader's post, which can be upgraded to a fur factory, is used to produce coats from furs. Once the colony's population has reached 6, it can be further upgraded to a fur factory, provided that Adam Smith has joined the Continental Congress. A fur trader's post increases coat production.

title: Fur factory
summary: The fur factory, which can not be upgraded, is used to produce coats from furs. A fur factory increased coat production.

title: Schoolhouse
summary: A colony with a population of at least 4 may build a schoolhouse, which enables some master craftsman to teach an unskilled colonist their trade. As soon as the population reaches 8, it can be upgraded to a college, in which additional trades can be taught by two colonists. Once the population reaches 10, the college can be replaced by a university, at which all trades can be taught by three colonists.\n\nA schoolhouse allows teaching skill faculty 1.

title: College
summary: A colony with a population of at least 4 may build a schoolhouse, which enables some master craftsman to teach an unskilled colonist their trade. As soon as the population reaches 8, it can be upgraded to a college, in which additional trades can be taught by two colonists. Once the population reaches 10, the college can be replaced by a university, at which all trades can be taught by three colonists.\n\nA college allows teaching skill faculty 2.

title: University
summary: A colony with a population of at least 4 may build a schoolhouse, which enables some master craftsman to teach an unskilled colonist their trade. As soon as the population reaches 8, it can be upgraded to a college, in which additional trades can be taught by two colonists. Once the population reaches 10, the college can be replaced by a university, at which all trades can be taught by three colonists.\n\nA university allows teaching skill faculty 3.

title: Armory
summary: The armory is used to produce muskets from tools. As soon as the population reaches 8, the armory can be upgraded to a magazine and then to an arsenal, provided that Adam Smith has joined the Continental Congress.\n\nAfter building an armory you are allowed to produce muskets and artillery.

title: Arsenal
summary: The arsenal is used to produce muskets from tools.\n\nAfter building an arsenal muskets only require half the number of tools to be produced.

title: Chapel
summary: The chapel is a place for your colonists to practice their religion. A chapel produces a small amount of crosses by itself, but no preacher may be put to work here. You will need to upgrade your chapel to a church first.

title: Church
summary: A colony with a population of 3 or more may build a church, which can be upgraded to a cathedral as soon as the population reaches 8. The religious freedom of the New World (symbolised by crosses) causes increased emigration from Europe.\n\nAfter building a church cross production increases and you are allowed to commission missionaries.

title: Cathedral
summary: A colony with a population of 3 or more may build a church, which can be upgraded to a cathedral as soon as the population reaches 8. The religious freedom of the New World (symbolised by crosses) causes increased emigration from Europe.\n\nAfter building a cathedral cross production increases.

title: Depot
summary: The depot stores all kinds of goods. Its initial capacity is 100 units of each kind of goods, but it can be upgraded to a warehouse, which holds 200. Building a further warehouse expansion increases storage capacities to 300.

title: Warehouse
summary: The warehouse stores all kinds of goods. It is the first upgrade of a depot, with a capacity of 200 units for each kind of goods. Building a warehouse expansion increases storage capacities to 300.

title: Warehouse expansion
summary: The expanded warehouse stores all kinds of goods. It is an upgrade to the simple warehouse, with a capacity of 300 units for each kind of goods.

title: Pasture
summary: The pasture is a place near your colony, where your horses roam freely. Building stables will increase the production of horses.

title: Stables
summary: The stables increase the maximum production of horses by reducing the size of herds.

title: Docks
summary: The dock allows colonists to produce fish on ocean tiles adjacent to the colony. As soon as the population is at least 4, it can be upgraded to a drydock, which allows the colony to repair damaged ships. When the colony's population reaches 8, it can be further upgraded to a shipyard, which enables the colony to build new ships.\n\nBuilding a dock allows fishing.

title: Drydock
summary: The drydock allows colonists to produce fish on ocean tiles adjacent to the colony, and it allows ship repair. When the colony's population reaches 8, it can be further upgraded to a shipyard, which enables the colony to build new ships.\n\nBuilding a drydock allows ship repair.

title: Shipyard
summary: The shipyard allows colonists to produce fish on ocean tiles adjacent to the colony, it allows ship repair, and it allows ship construction.\n\nBuilding a shipyard allows ship construction.

title: Printing press
summary: The printing press, which can be upgraded to a newspaper as soon as the population reaches 4, increases the colony's production of liberty bells.

title: Newspaper
summary: The newspaper, which can only be built after building a printing press and as soon the population reaches 4, increases liberty bell production.

title: Custom house
summary: The custom house, which can be built as soon as Peter Stuyvesant has joined the Continental Congress, allows the colony to export goods to Europe directly without the help of ships. Also, it allows trading with foreign powers after the declaration of independence. Optionally, it may also ignore boycotts.

title: Adam Smith
summary: Enables building of factories.
text: Better known as the Father of Modern Economics, Smith penned several texts pertaining to Economic theory, including, The Wealth of Nations his most famous text.

title: Jacob Fugger II
summary: All boycotts currently in effect are dropped.
text: Extremely wealthy German merchant and banker. Amassed a fortune with family partnerships and Stock holdings in the mining industries.

title: Peter Minuit
summary: Indians no longer demand payment for their land.
text: Bought what later became known as Manhattan Island from Native Americans for about 60 Dutch guilders. He later would colonise the Delaware Bay area as well.

title: Peter Stuyvesant
summary: The construction of custom houses becomes possible.
text: Appointed Governor General of New Netherlands which, after a British invasion he could not stop, became New York.

title: Jan de Witt
summary: Trade with foreign colonies becomes possible and more information about colonial rivals is displayed.
text: De Witt was a great Dutch statesmen. He represented the merchants and encouraged industry and commerce. He also negotiated several important treaties for the Dutch to end wars with England.

title: Ferdinand Magellan
summary: Naval vessels movement is increased by 1 and the time to sail to/from Europe/America is shortened.
text: One of the greatest explorers to navigate the globe. Magellan was first to circumnavigate the globe and cross the Pacific Ocean.

title: Francisco de Coronado
summary: All existing colonies become visible on the map.
text: First European explorer to see the Grand Canyon. Though he never found the golden cities he searched for, his mapping of the area now called the Southwestern U.S. was important to further exploration.

title: Hernando de Soto
summary: Exploration of Lost City Rumours never yields a negative result and all land units have an extended sight radius.
text: First European to explore Florida and the southeastern U.S. He also held a prominent role in conquests of Central America.

title: Henry Hudson
text: English Navigator who explored and mapped a large area of the northeastern North American continent.  Many waterways in that region are named in his honour.  His original goal was to find the famed Northwest Passage.

title: Robert de La Salle
summary: Gives all existing and future colonies a stockade when their population reaches 3.
text: The first European to travel the length of the Mississippi river, de La Salle was on a mission to set up numerous trading posts along its banks. He later claimed the whole basin as Louisiana in honour of the French King. Later, he explored several of the Great Lakes.

title: Hernan Cortes
summary: Conquered native settlements always yield treasure (and in greater abundance) and the monarch's galleons transport it free of charge.
text: Famed Spanish conquistador who overthrew the Aztec Empire and claimed Mexico for Spain.

title: George Washington
summary: Any soldier or dragoon who wins a combat is automatically upgraded to the next possible level.
text: General Washington lead the colonial army to victory over the British to gain independence for the colonies. This victory and his leadership led to his being named the new nation's first President.

title: Paul Revere
summary: When a colony with no standing soldiers is attacked, a colonist automatically takes up any stockpiled muskets and defends.
text: The famed rider of colonial America mounted his horse and rode through the countryside alerting colonists that British soldiers were coming. He was captured during the ride and later released when his captors believed they were in grave danger and their prisoner might slow them down.

title: Francis Drake
text: A great English sea captain, Drake was the first Englishman to circumnavigate the globe and a hero in the fights against the Spanish Armada.

title: John Paul Jones
summary: A Frigate is added to your colonial navy (free).
text: Hailed as a great sea captain in America, Jones uttered the famous words `Sir, I have not yet begun to fight' while fighting the British at sea. He later watched his ship sink to the bottom of the ocean from the deck of a British vessel.

title: Thomas Jefferson
text: A powerful voice of Patriotism, Jefferson was credited with writing the Declaration of Independence. He later became the 3rd President of the U.S.

title: Pocahontas
summary: All tension levels between you and natives are removed and Indian alarm is generated half as fast.
text: A peacemaker between early Jamestown settlers and the Native Americans. She is credited with sending food and other supplies to starving colonists there during harsh times. She later converted to Christianity and married an Englishman.

title: Thomas Paine
summary: Increases Liberty Bell production in colonies by the value of the current tax rate.
text: Inspired colonists with his pen at the urging of Benjamin Franklin. Publish a pamphlet, Common Sense, guiding the thoughts of patriots all over the colonies.

title: Simon Bolivar
text: Remembered as a great leader in the struggle for South American independence from Spain. Bolivar freed what is now Venezuela and later became its first President.

title: Benjamin Franklin
summary: The Crown's foreign wars no longer have effect on relationships in the New World and Europeans in the New World always offer peace in negotiations.
text: A heavy contributor to the Declaration of Independence, Franklin was one of the voices of the Revolution. He travelled extensively between Europe and the colonies gainined the support of the French in the war.

title: William Brewster
summary: No more criminals or servants appear on the docks, and you can select which immigrant in the recruitment pool to move to the docks.
text: Brewster was the Puritan leader of the Plymouth colony in New England.

title: William Penn
text: As a close friend of the Duke of York, Penn was granted the land that is mostly Pennsylvania, Delaware, and New Jersey. He Governed the Quaker colony for several years to provide a haven to fellow Quakers.

title: Father Jean de Brebeuf
summary: All missionaries function as experts.
text: Befriended the Huron Indians and converted many to Christianity. Died at the hands of the Iroquois who had finally defeated their enemy, the Hurons.

title: Juan de Sepulveda
text: A Spanish theologian who spoke out for the conquest of Indian lands and forced evangelisation of the natives.

title: Bartolome de las Casas
summary: All existing Indian converts are converted to free colonists.
text: A Catholic Priest who traveled the Indies converting Indians and chastising Spain for their treatment of the Natives.
